description: Get a crew with its recent chat messages (the crew output) and operator comments. Use this to see what a crew produced and where it stands. The crew leads with `status`, `currentNode`, the halt or error reason (`haltCode`, `errorCode`, `errorMessage`), `pendingPermissionRequest`, its work item, initiative, `prUrl` and timestamps; these are never left out. By default (`shape: "summary"`) text over 1,000 characters is excerpted and named in `excerptedFields`, and any other value over 2,000 characters (the skill, decision-context and execution-memory snapshots) is left out and named with its size in `omittedFields`; chat and comment entries get the same treatment one by one, each naming its own. For status only, pass `messages: 0`: a few KB. Pass `shape: "full"` only when you need a left-out field in full; a full crew can run past 70,000 characters. When the repository uses AWS CodeArtifact the crew also carries `codeArtifactAttempt`: why a registry token was or was not issued (failing AWS call, missing permission, the stored key's identity). The returned crew carries `url` — its Console page; when you show the crew to the user, render its id/name as a link to that url. Reviewer verdicts (`architectVerdict`, `securityVerdict`, `qaVerdict`) come with `<field>Label`, the word the Console shows, and `<field>Outcome` (`clean`, `non_blocking` or `blocking`). `NEEDS_REVISION` is non-blocking and the Console labels it "Advisory"; the Console's "Needs revision" means the blocking `FAIL`.

messages.description: How many recent chat and comment entries, newest kept and returned oldest first (default 20 with shape "summary", 50 with "full"; max 200). Pass 0 for a status read: it skips the chat and comment reads.

shape.description: summary (default): lead fields first, long text excerpted, large values left out and named. full: every field as stored.

title: Get crew
